resolutions.implementation: A separate AudioPreviewLease holds desired output across every phrase/rest until preview teardown. SongPlayback awaits and synchronously validates initial lease/click readiness and every subsequent note readiness. The lease records the prepared output revision: any lost/restarted graph or failed note ends the preview through finished(), rather than advancing or repeatedly re-anchoring musical time over hardware stalls. Cancellation cancels owned note/click handles and releases only its lease; outro ownership remains independent.

Raw Task<Bool> command handles are replaced by AudioReadiness: an awaited result plus a synchronous current command/transport ownership predicate and consume(action). AudioStartGate executes consume immediately on MainActor before clock/cue/band callbacks. Preview consumers synchronously check lease and note identities after each await; recording sync uses the same gate. Recording schedule preserves the request generation instead of silently advancing it under the readiness token.

InterfaceSoundPlayback awaits session preparation on MainActor, then invokes the synchronous metadata predicate and actual player preparation/play without another await or task hop. AudioSessionOwner.interfaceSoundMayPlayNow reads only fast lock-protected metadata. AudioService and RecordingPlayer reserve foreground ownership synchronously when desired intent is recorded, before creating asynchronous activation tasks; release remains balanced through pending activation completion. No queue.sync/hardware wait is restored.

Published playbackRequested describes pending-or-playing UI intent, while isPlaying remains the actual clock state. The dock button appearance, accessibility label, and shared toggleRecordingPlayback action use playbackRequested. A second tap pauses/cancels pending transport instead of adding another play request.

additional_review_observations: Corrected RecordingPlayer class comment: configuration changes pause pending the next play; automatic route continuation is not claimed.
Pause during pending seek now retains the synchronously recorded requested target; testPauseDuringPendingSeekPreservesTheRequestedTarget covers this with delayed activation.
